title: Finite enriched horn-cell filtration for coherent simplex thickenings
statement: Use simplicial sets, simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the subset-poset simplicial categories $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. For any small simplicial set $K$, put $\mathfrak C[K]=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^r\to K}\mathfrak C[\Delta^r]$, with colimit in simplicial categories. For a simplicial set $X$, let $U(X)$ have two objects $a,b$, morphism simplicial sets $U(X)(a,b)=X$, $U(X)(b,a)=\varnothing$, and both endomorphism simplicial sets $\Delta^0$, with composition specified by identities. For $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$, the induced enriched functor $\mathfrak C[\Lambda_i^n]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ admits a finite filtration by pushouts in simplicial categories. Every successive attaching map is a finite coproduct of maps $U(\Lambda_j^m)\to U(\Delta^m)$ induced by horn inclusions, where $m\geq1$ and $0\leq j\leq m$; all stages have the object set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and the transition functors are the identity on objects.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.8 (00LR), the enriched inner-horn inclusion and its hollow-cube mapping object; Corollary 2.4.5.10 (00LT) for extension through that mapping object, and Corollary 2.4.5.12 (00LV) for the box inclusion. The finite free-horn filtration is the combinatorial triangulation refinement of this box calculation, stated here as an agent-specified support lemma. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$. Work with the inclusion-ordered subset convention of the cited definition. In simplicial degree $r$, a morphism $p\to q$, $p<q$, of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is a chain $\{p,q\}\subseteq S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_r\subseteq[p,q]$. Composition is termwise union. Write $S_0=\{v_0=p<\cdots<v_t=q\}$. Intersecting every $S_a$ with each interval $[v_{h-1},v_h]$ factors this morphism into $t$ chains whose first subset is exactly their two endpoints. This factorization is unique: a termwise union of such chains has as its first subset exactly their endpoints, so the factor endpoints must be the successive elements of $S_0$, and intersecting with their intervals recovers each factor. Hence this degree category is freely generated by the chains with $S_0=\{p,q\}$, with identity arrows at the vertices.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.8 proof, degreewise path generators; translated to the inclusion-ordered subset convention and with the unique factorization written out.

proof.text: For a simplicial subset $T\subseteq\Delta^n$ containing all vertices, the simplex-colimit defining $\mathfrak C[T]$ can be computed over its nondegenerate faces: every simplex has a unique surjection onto its image face, so a cocone on these faces extends uniquely to all simplices by that surjection. In degree $r$, each face category has the free generators of step 1 whose last subset $S_r$ is contained in that face. A face inclusion preserves these generators, and every generator already occurs in its smallest face $S_r$. Consequently maps from the face diagram into any degree category are exactly assignments to the generators whose support $S_r$ is a face of $T$, with a common assignment to vertices. Extending an assignment to words gives the required unique functor, proving the free-category colimit property directly. These degreewise categories form a simplicial category: deletion or repetition in a chain, followed by the unique factorization of step 1, describes each simplicial operator; this is the operator on any face containing the support, so it is independent of the face and satisfies the simplicial identities. The same generator argument for functors compatible with those operators proves the enriched colimit universal property. Thus $\mathfrak C[T]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is identity on vertices and injective on mapping simplicial sets; its degree-$r$ image consists of words in the generators with support a face of $T$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.8 proof; explicit simplex-colimit and free-generator mapping-out computation, with no Kan or model-category input.

proof.text:
Take $T=\Lambda_i^n$. By the cited horn definition, a support is allowed exactly when it omits a vertex of $[n]$ other than $i$. If $(p,q)
e(0,n)$ and $p<q$, the interval $[p,q]$ omits $0$ or $n$, both different from $i$; therefore all its generators are allowed. Identities and empty reverse mapping sets also agree. For a chain from $0$ to $n$, step 1 says that if $S_0$ contains an interior vertex then every factor has a proper interval as its support range, so every factor is allowed. If $S_0=\{0,n\}$, the chain is a single generator and is allowed exactly when $S_r$ omits an interior vertex other than $i$. Put $D=\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $J_a=S_a\setminus\{0,n\}$. Thus the exceptional mapping inclusion is precisely $A\subseteq Q=N(\mathcal P(D))=(\Delta^1)^D$, where its chains satisfy
$$J_0
e\varnothing\quad	ext{or}\quad D\setminus\{i\}
subseteq J_r.$$
Here $\mathcal P(D)$ is the inclusion poset of subsets and the product identification sends a subset to its characteristic function; weak chains give the identification in every degree and commute with every operator.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.8(a)-(c); explicit support test. The coordinate convention is the inclusion-poset convention of the project, rather than Kerodon’s complementary coordinates.

proof.text:
Let $B=(\Delta^1)^{D\setminus\{i\}}$ and let $\partial B$ be the union of its coordinate-$0$ and coordinate-$1$ faces, with the empty union $\partial B=\varnothing$ when $D=\{i\}$. Use coordinate $i$ as the first factor to identify $Q=\Delta^1\times B$. For a weak chain, $J_0\ne\varnothing$ means some coordinate is constantly $1$, and $D\setminus\{i\}\nsubseteq J_r$ means some coordinate other than $i$ is constantly $0$. These alternatives give exactly
$$ A=(\{1\}\times B)\cup(\Delta^1\times\partial B). $$
The nondegenerate simplices of $B$ are the strict chains in the finite subset poset $\mathcal P(D\setminus\{i\})$, so there are finitely many. List those not in $\partial B$ in increasing dimension, breaking ties arbitrarily. Starting at $B_0=\partial B$, adjoin them successively to get $B_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq B_s=B$. Each $k$-simplex on this list is embedded, all its proper faces occur earlier or in $\partial B$, and its interior has not occurred: no distinct simplex of dimension at most $k$ can contain this strict chain. Hence its intersection with the preceding stage is exactly $\partial\Delta^k$, and the corresponding union is its boundary pushout, degree by degree.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.5.12, displayed box union, with the finite base-chain filtration made explicit in project coordinates.

proof.text: Set $P_\ell=(\{1\}\times B)\cup(\Delta^1\times B_\ell)$, so $P_0=A$ and $P_s=Q$. For an embedded simplex $\sigma:\Delta^k\to B$ added at stage $\ell$, the preimage of $P_{\ell-1}$ under $\mathrm{id}\times\sigma$ is exactly $(\{1\}\times\Delta^k)\cup(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^k)$, by the intersection computed in step 4. Its union with $P_{\ell-1}$ is $P_\ell$, so this is a pushout. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] with $m=k$ and push out each of its $k+1$ squares along this intersection. The result refines $P_{\ell-1}\subseteq P_\ell$ into $k+1$ pushouts of $\Lambda_{q+1}^{k+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{k+1}$, $0\leq q\leq k$. To check that the pushed-out squares are the claimed unions, maps on the old stage and on an attached simplex agreeing on its horn glue uniquely in each degree, and commute with simplicial operators because both pieces do. There are finitely many base simplices, so concatenating these refinements gives a finite horn-pushout filtration $A=Y_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Y_N=Q$. All horn dimensions are positive, including $k=0$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.12, the exact finite boundary-prism filtration supplied by the existing node; base-chain refinement and gluing expanded here.

proof.text: For each $A\subseteq Y\subseteq Q$ from step 5, define $E_Y$ to have objects $0,\ldots,n$, endpoint mapping set $E_Y(0,n)=Y$, and every other mapping set that of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$. Give it the inherited compositions. This is a subcategory: every composition through an interior vertex $v$ lands in the endpoint face where coordinate $v$ is constantly $1$, which is contained in $A\subseteq Y$; a composition using $Y$ as an input has as its other input an identity, since the ordered category has no nonidentity arrows into $0$ or out of $n$. Associativity and units are inherited from termwise union. Steps 2-4 identify $E_A$ with $\mathfrak C[\Lambda_i^n]$ over $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, and $E_Q=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.9; explicit intermediate enriched categories and composition checks in the subset-poset model.

proof.text: Suppose a step $Y\subseteq Y'$ of step 5 attaches $\Delta^m$ along $\Lambda_j^m$. Send the two objects of $U(\Lambda_j^m)$ and $U(\Delta^m)$ to $0,n$. We verify that the resulting square with bottom row $E_Y\to E_{Y'}$ is an enriched pushout. For any target simplicial category $H$, compatible functors from $E_Y$ and $U(\Delta^m)$ specify a functor $F:E_Y\to H$ and a simplicial map $\Delta^m\to H(F0,Fn)$ agreeing with $F$ on the attaching horn. The simplicial pushout gives a unique map $Y'\to H(F0,Fn)$ extending them. Keep $F$ on objects and on all other mapping sets. Composition is preserved: with the new endpoint mapping set as an input, the other input is an identity; without it as an input, the only changed-output case is a composition through an interior vertex, which already lands in $A\subseteq Y$ and satisfies the old functor equation. Thus these data define a unique enriched functor $E_{Y'}\to H$, proving the pushout universal property. This works also when $F0=Fn$. Apply this at every step of the finite filtration. Each attaching map is a singleton finite coproduct of the required $U$-horn maps, all stages have the specified object set, and their transition functors are identity on objects. This proves every clause.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.5.9, full composition check; universal-property proof of each enriched U-horn pushout, followed by finite induction.

lean.statement: theorem exists_coherent_nerve_cell_filtration (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hi : 0 < i.val) (hin : i.val < n) : ∃ (N : ℕ) (F : ComposableArrows SCat.{u} N) (e : ∀ l : Fin (N + 1), (F.obj l : Type u) ≃ Fin (n + 1)) (h₀ : F.left = Pinched.rigidification.obj (horn n i)) (hN : F.right = Pinched.rigidification.obj (Δ[n])), F.hom = eqToHom h₀ ≫ Pinched.rigidification.map (horn n i).ι ≫ eqToHom hN.symm ∧ (∀ x : (horn n i).toSSet _⦋0⦌, e 0 ((eqToHom h₀.symm).obj (Pinched.vertex (horn n i) x)) = stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv ((horn n i).ι.app (op ⦋0⦌) x)) ∧ (∀ j : Fin (n + 1), e (Fin.last N) ((eqToHom hN.symm).obj (Pinched.vertex Δ[n] (stdSimplex.obj₀Equiv.symm j))) = j) ∧ (∀ l : Fin N, ∀ x : F.obj l.castSucc, e l.succ ((F.map' l.val (l.val + 1)).obj x) = e l.castSucc x) ∧ (∀ l : Fin N, ∃ (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → ℕ) (j : ∀ t : Fin r, Fin (m t + 1)), (∀ t : Fin r, 1 ≤ m t) ∧ ∃ (p : (∐ fun t : Fin r ↦ Bergner.bundle (Bergner.U.{u} (horn (m t) (j t)))) ⟶ F.obj l.castSucc) (q : (∐ fun t : Fin r ↦ Bergner.bundle (Bergner.U.{u} Δ[m t])) ⟶ F.obj l.succ), IsPushout (Limits.Sigma.map (C := SCat.{u}) (fun t : Fin r ↦ Bergner.bundleMap.{u} (Bergner.uMap.{u} (horn (m t) (j t)).ι))) p q (F.map' l.val (l.val + 1)))
